text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AN-NAHAR
-Lebanon's cargo carrier Trans Mediterranean Airlines decided to increase capital to 60 billion Lebanese pounds through the issue of 59,994,000 shares of 1,000 pounds each.
-Lebanon and Syria boycott Cairo economic summit arguing that normalisation of relations with Israel should not take place before the prospects of peace are clear.
-Security sources expect the release of missing Israeli pilot Ron Arad soon. Arad is the only one among four Israeli soldiers who went missing in Lebanon in the 1980s believed to be alive.
-The Lebanese foreign ministry raises the issue of Lebanese families expelled from Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone recently with the ambassadors of the United States and France.
-The new cabinet will meet for the first time today to discuss the government's policy statement.
-The Constitutional Council begins today discussing appeals from 19 defeated candidates against the results of recent parliamentary elections.
-Hizbollah chief Sheikh Nasrallah says the group had 1,145 "martyrs" since 1982 in confrontations with Israeli and allied militia forces in south Lebanon.
AS-SAFIR
-Housing Minister Abu Hamdan says 10,000 housing units will be built soon for Lebanese with limited income.

-Escalation in south Lebanon between Hizbollah and Israeli forces. Israeli planes raided the Hizbollah-controlled hills of Iqlim al-Toufah after two weekend guerrilla attacks in which one Israeli soldier was killed and six wounded.
-The northern port of Tripoli finds a solution for its garbage disposal problems by deciding to bury the garbage on the beach.
-President Hrawi to officially reopen the Casino du Liban on December 3 after a stoppage of more than 20 years.
AL-ANWAR
-An official of the ministry of posts and communications says Lebanon will decrease rates on international telephone calls by 15 percent and raise them on local ones.
-Lebanon's oldest person died last week at 125 years of age.
AD-DIYAR

-Druze leader and minister for displaced people Jumblatt sees the cabinet's policy statement as a ground for a confrontation with Prime Minister Hariri. Jumblatt, who has waged recent attacks on Hariri, said: "The (new) government will not last long".
NIDA'A AL-WATAN
-Former director general of the finance ministry Khattar Shibli expresses fears that Lebanon's public debt will rise to 20,000 billion Lebanese pounds by the end of 1997.
